# DECISIONS

## 1. What "trustworthy" means here
Chose: advice and behavior must come from the same source of truth â€” anywhere the system tells a reviewer "this submission is below the floor" it must also act (or refuse to act) on that same floor. Rejected: a broader redesign of the promote UX; the timebox points at the divergence, not a rebuild.

## 2. Root divergence identified
Traced the promote path end-to-end: the orchestrator's ranked stage promotes against `activePromoteFloor()` (calibrated dev_control floor, else `DEV_POLICY.promoteFloor` = 55). The manual route `app/api/devcase/promote/route.ts` never consulted any floor â€” it promoted any evaluated submission. So the UI could advise "hold, below floor" while a click promoted anyway. Fixed this first as the highest-trust-impact divergence.

## 3. Enforce in the route, not in promoteSubmission
Chose: keep `promoteSubmission` floor-agnostic (pure mechanism) and enforce policy at both call sites via the shared `activePromoteFloor()`. Rejected: pushing the floor check into `promoteSubmission` itself â€” that would double-check the orchestrator's already-filtered ranked list and change semantics for any future policy-exempt caller.

## 4. Human override with audit, not a hard block
Chose: below-floor manual promotion returns 409 with `overridable: true`; passing `override: true` promotes and writes a `promote_override_below_floor` row to the immutable `dev_audit` log. Rejected: a hard block â€” humans legitimately outrank the calibrated floor (e.g. strong live-session signal); trust needs the override visible, not impossible.

## 5. Unscored evaluations pass through
Chose: if the evaluation has no numeric score, skip the floor check and promote (previous behavior), while still auditing. Rejected: failing closed on missing score â€” that would silently break legacy evaluations, and the brief asked for consistency, not new gates.

## 6. Verification approach
Added `route.test.ts` covering: below-floor hold (409), at-floor promote, explicit override + audit row, calibrated-floor (non-default) enforcement, and unscored pass-through. Other callers checked: the orchestrator's ranked stage already filters by `activePromoteFloor()` before calling `promoteSubmission`, so it is unaffected; the outcomes/calibration route reads the same shared helper, so displayed and enforced floors stay identical. Ran the suite and a typecheck; all green.

solutions.note: Aligned the manual promote route with the orchestrator's calibrated floor (shared activePromoteFloor), added an audited human override, and verified with route-level tests.
